subject.title: The Skill Accumulation Problem: How many skills before your agent gets confused?

question: Should ClawHub add a first-class skill-governance surface for task-context recommendations, conflict/dependency metadata, and local load policy, and which boundary should own each part?
rationale: Current main only implements adjacent discovery and pinning pieces; the remaining behavior changes public metadata, privacy boundaries, and possibly OpenClaw runtime loading semantics, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Define a governance contract first
options.body: Write the intended recommendation, conflict, privacy, and runtime/load-policy boundary in specs before implementing schema/API/UI/CLI changes.

options.title: Limit this to guidance
options.body: Keep ClawHub's product surface unchanged and answer the issue with documented best practices for pruning, layering, and pinning skills.

options.title: Split runtime work out
options.body: Track only ClawHub metadata/search pieces here and require a separate OpenClaw runtime proposal for priority and tool-collision enforcement.

recommendation.title: Define a governance contract first
recommendation.body: Write the intended recommendation, conflict, privacy, and runtime/load-policy boundary in specs before implementing schema/API/UI/CLI changes.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses CODEOWNERS-protected schema/API/CLI surfaces and needs someone already tied to those contracts.
